iterations.theme: Centar za život u Splitu: pomoć trudnicama i osobama ranjenima pobačajem, duhovna pozadina pobačaja i mijenjanje svijesti društva

sections.subtitle: Od molitve pred bolnicom do centra koji mijenja živote
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić predstavlja sebe i rad Centra za život u Splitu
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta **Mreže Riječi** otvara se kratkim uvodnim isječkom. Nepoznati sugovornik izgovara rečenicu „Nisam bio nesretan. Nijedan dan nisam bio nesretan.“, a odmah zatim čuje se i kratki pozdrav „Bona sera“. Nakon toga voditelj **Slavko Blažić** pozdravlja gledatelje i predstavlja gošću. Riječ je o **Mariji Šošić**, voditeljici Splitskog centra za život. Ona je i dobitnica nagrade Splitsko-dalmatinske županije za iznimni doprinos u zaštiti nerođene djece.

Na pitanje tko je ona, Marija Šošić odgovara da je *najprije supruga*, a tek zatim voditeljica Centra za život u Splitu. Centar u gradu djeluje šest godina. Ona je pak već **12 godina uključena u Apostolat za život**, odnosno u promicanje kulture života i zaštitu života od začeća do prirodne smrti. Taj rad, kako navodi, provodi se kroz inicijativu **„40 dana za život“**.

Voditelja zanima je li inicijativa dio Centra. Gošća pojašnjava da je redoslijed bio obrnut. Inicijativa „40 dana za život“ pokrenuta je prije 12 godina, najprije u Zagrebu, a potom u Splitu i drugim gradovima diljem Hrvatske. Već su se na samim počecima javljale trudnice kojima nije bila potrebna samo savjetodavna, nego i materijalna pomoć. Zato je trebalo pronaći način za prikupljanje donacija i pružanje pomoći, pa je osnovana krovna udruga **„Hrvatska za život“**.

Kroz tu udrugu djeluje više programa, a jedan od njih je i Centar za život. Nastao je jer je bio potreban prostor za razgovore i provođenje svih programa udruge. Centar danas ima dvostruku ulogu:
- **savjetovalište za trudnice**
- **Središnji ured inicijative „40 dana za život“**
sections.subtitle_en: From prayer in front of the hospital to a center that changes lives
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić introduces herself and the work of the Center for Life in Split
sections.content_en:
The episode of the podcast **Mreže Riječi** opens with a short introductory clip. An unknown interlocutor utters the sentence "I was not unhappy. Not a single day was I unhappy.", and immediately following that, a brief greeting "Bona sera" is also heard. After that, host **Slavko Blažić** greets the viewers and introduces the guest. It is **Marija Šošić**, head of the Split Center for Life. She is also the recipient of the Split-Dalmatia County Award for exceptional contribution to the protection of unborn children.

To the question of who she is, Marija Šošić replies that she is *first and foremost a wife*, and only then the head of the Center for Life in Split. The Center has been operating in the city for six years. She, however, has already been **involved in the Apostolate for Life for 12 years**, namely in promoting the culture of life and protecting life from conception to natural death. That work, as she states, is carried out through the initiative **"40 Days for Life"**.

The host is interested in whether the initiative is part of the Center. The guest clarifies that the order was reversed. The "40 Days for Life" initiative was launched 12 years ago, first in Zagreb, and then in Split and other cities across Croatia. Already at the very beginnings, pregnant women were reaching out who needed not only counseling, but also material assistance. Therefore, a way had to be found to collect donations and provide assistance, so the umbrella association **"Hrvatska za život"** was founded.

Through that association, several programs operate, and one of them is the Center for Life. It was created because space was needed for conversations and the implementation of all the association's programs. The Center today has a dual role:
- **counseling center for pregnant women**
- **Central Office of the "40 Days for Life" initiative**

sections.subtitle: Svaka majka, jedna priča: stručnjaci, grupe podrške i krunice koje vraćaju samopouzdanje
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća opisuje trenutak kad majka u suzama drži prvu krunicu koju je sama izradila
sections.content:
Slavko Blažić pita koji su najvažniji programi Centra. Marija Šošić na prvo mjesto stavlja **rad s trudnicama i majkama**. Posebno ističe one koje su razmišljale o pobačaju, dobile pomoć i odlučile se za život. One su, kako kaže, najčešći posjetitelji Centra.

Pristup je strogo **individualan**. „Koliko god imamo majki, koliko god ima trudnica, toliko ima priča“, objašnjava gošća. Centar svaku majku povezuje sa stručnjacima koji su joj u tom trenutku potrebni:
- svećenicima
- psiholozima i psihijatrima
- odvjetnicima
- socijalnim radnicima
- drugim profesijama koje majci mogu pomoći da *samostalno zaplovi u život*

Uz razgovore i stručnu pomoć Centar organizira **grupe podrške** i **radionice**. Radionice su kreativne, ali i terapijske. Cilj im je da se majka osjeća prihvaćeno i korisno, te da kroz rad vlastitim rukama doživi da je napravila nešto dobro.

Najčešće su **radionice izrade krunica**. Na njima majke rade zajedno s volonterkama, a one koje su vjernice dolaze i na molitvu krunice. Marija Šošić opisuje prizor kojem je svjedočila nekoliko puta. Majka na početku tvrdi da krunicu nikako neće uspjeti napraviti jer je postupak presložen. Kad joj pomognu da ga dovede do kraja i ugleda gotovu krunicu u rukama, počne plakati. Objašnjenje je, kaže gošća, uvijek slično: „Pa mene su učili da ja ništa ne mogu, da ja ništa ne znam, da ne vrijedim. A evo, stvorila sam nešto svojim rukama.“

Krunice imaju i praktičnu svrhu. Uzimaju ih dobročinitelji, a zauzvrat Centar dobiva donacije. Marija Šošić naglašava da **upravo od tih donacija Centar i udruga jedino žive**. Uz krunice se održavaju i radionice zlatoveza te tematske kreativne radionice za Dan života, Božić, Uskrs i rođendan Centra.
sections.subtitle_en: Every mother, one story: experts, support groups, and Rosaries that restore self-confidence
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the moment when a mother in tears holds the first Rosary she made herself
sections.content_en:
Slavko Blažić asks what the most important programs of the Center are. Marija Šošić puts **work with pregnant women and mothers** in first place. She particularly highlights those who were considering abortion, received help, and chose life. They are, as she says, the most frequent visitors to the Center.

The approach is strictly **individual**. "However many mothers we have, however many pregnant women there are, that is how many stories there are," explains the guest. The Center connects each mother with the experts she needs at that moment:
- priests
- psychologists and psychiatrists
- lawyers
- social workers
- other professions that can help the mother to *sail independently into life*

Along with conversations and professional help, the Center organizes **support groups** and **workshops**. The workshops are creative, but also therapeutic. Their goal is for the mother to feel accepted and useful, and through work with her own hands to experience that she has made something good.

The most frequent are **Rosary making workshops**. In them, mothers work together with female volunteers, and those who are believers also come to Rosary prayer. Marija Šošić describes a scene she has witnessed several times. A mother at the beginning claims that she will by no means succeed in making a Rosary because the process is too complex. When they help her bring it to completion and she beholds the finished Rosary in her hands, she begins to cry. The explanation, says the guest, is always similar: "Why, they taught me that I can do nothing, that I know nothing, that I am worthless. And behold, I created something with my own hands."

The Rosaries also have a practical purpose. Benefactors take them, and in return the Center receives donations. Marija Šošić emphasizes that **it is precisely from these donations that the Center and the association exclusively live**. Along with Rosaries, gold embroidery workshops and themed creative workshops are also held for the Day of Life, Christmas, Easter, and the Center's birthday.

sections.subtitle: Bol koja ne prolazi: majke i očevi ranjeni pobačajem
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić prenosi riječi majki koje desetljećima razmišljaju o svom nerođenom djetetu
sections.content:
Marija Šošić ističe da u Centar ne dolaze samo trudnice u dvojbi. Često dolaze i **majke i očevi koji su već ranjeni pobačajem**. Prva zadaća udruge jest skrb za one koji o pobačaju tek razmišljaju. Zato su molitelji pred bolnicom, gdje su, kako kaže, „živi znak nade“ i „jedna živa reklama“ da se ljudi mogu obratiti za pomoć.

S vremenom su se počeli javljati i drugi. Gošća prenosi njihove riječi: „Dobro, vi pomažete tim ženama, to je divno, vrijedno i pohvalno, ali što je s nama? Za nas više nema natrag.“ Neki su pobačaj doživjeli prije 20 ili 30 godina, a i dalje ne mogu zaboraviti. Razmišljaju kakvo bi njihovo dijete bilo, kakve bi oči imalo, bi li bio dječak ili djevojčica. Mnogi to ne znaju jer se pobačaj dogodio u ranoj fazi trudnoće, kad spol obično još nije poznat.

Razgovori su često vrlo emotivni. Gošća slikovito kaže da su **papirnate maramice najčešći rekvizit** koji se u Centru troši na dnevnoj bazi. Žene osjećaju da ih nitko ne razumije i da se njihova bol umanjuje. Mnoge tek u Centru prvi put nekome ispričaju što su doživjele. Neke o tome, osim liječnika koji je obavio zahvat, nisu rekle ni suprugu ni obitelji.

Olakšanje dolazi kad bol mogu izreći u intimnoj atmosferi s jamstvom diskrecije i bez osude. S druge strane ih ne dočekuje „E, kako si mogla…“, nego ljubav, podrška i, kako kaže Marija Šošić, **most do milosrdne Božje ljubavi** koja rado prašta svakome tko to zatraži.

Iskustvo je pokazalo da jedan razgovor i jedna ispovijed nisu dovoljni, iako je **ispovijed pobačaja najvažniji korak** u cijelom procesu. Neke su žene pobačaj ispovjedile više puta, iako to nije potrebno. Slavko Blažić to povezuje s krivnjom koja čovjeka tjera da se stalno vraća na učinjeno. Gošća potvrđuje: ženu progoni krivnja. Teško prihvaća da joj je Bog oprostio i da su joj oprostili i drugi sudionici pobačaja.

A sudionika je, prema njezinim riječima, uvijek više:
- liječnik i medicinsko osoblje
- onaj tko je platio zahvat
- onaj tko je ženu odveo ili na nju vršio pritisak
- pa čak i onaj tko je znao, a šutio i uskratio podršku
sections.subtitle_en: Pain that does not pass: mothers and fathers wounded by abortion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić conveys the words of mothers who for decades have been thinking about their unborn child
sections.content_en:
Marija Šošić points out that not only pregnant women in doubt come to the Center. Frequently, **mothers and fathers who are already wounded by abortion** also come. The first task of the association is care for those who are only just considering abortion. That is why the prayer warriors are in front of the hospital, where they are, as she says, a "living sign of hope" and "a living advertisement" that people can turn for help.

Over time, others began to reach out as well. The guest conveys their words: "Fine, you help those women, that is wonderful, valuable, and commendable, but what about us? For us there is no going back anymore." Some experienced abortion 20 or 30 years ago, and still cannot forget. They wonder what their child would be like, what kind of eyes they would have, whether it would be a boy or a girl. Many do not know this because the abortion occurred in an early stage of pregnancy, when the sex is usually not yet known.

The conversations are often very emotional. The guest vividly says that **paper tissues are the most common prop** consumed in the Center on a daily basis. Women feel that no one understands them and that their pain is being minimized. Many tell someone what they experienced for the first time only at the Center. Some, apart from the physician who performed the procedure, have told neither their husband nor their family about it.

Relief comes when they can utter the pain in an intimate atmosphere with a guarantee of discretion and without condemnation. On the other side, they are not greeted with "Well, how could you…", but with love, support, and, as Marija Šošić says, **a bridge to God's merciful love** that gladly forgives everyone who asks for it.

Experience has shown that one conversation and one confession are not enough, although **confession of abortion is the most important step** in the whole process. Some women have confessed abortion multiple times, even though that is not necessary. Slavko Blažić connects this with guilt that drives a person to constantly return to what was done. The guest confirms: guilt haunts the woman. She finds it hard to accept that God has forgiven her and that the other participants in the abortion have forgiven her as well.

And participants, according to her words, are always multiple:
- the physician and medical staff
- the one who paid for the procedure
- the one who took the woman or exerted pressure on her
- and even the one who knew, but remained silent and withheld support

sections.subtitle: „Oprostom oslobođene“: od rane do molitve za druge majke
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava program duhovno-psihološke pomoći „Oprostom oslobođene“
sections.content:
Za žene ranjene pobačajem Centar je pokrenuo program **„Oprostom oslobođene“**. Marija Šošić ga opisuje kao **duhovno-psihološku pomoć** koja se provodi u obliku duhovnih vježbi. Žene razmatraju Božju riječ i pristupaju sakramentalnom životu. Tako dolaze do iskustva oslobađajućeg Božjeg milosrđa i mogu, kako kaže, „živjeti u slobodi Djeteta Božjega“.

Nakon programa mnoge se aktivno uključuju u **Apostolat za život**. Najčešće se pridružuju moliteljima pred bolnicom i mole za drugu djecu i majke u situaciji u kojoj su nekad bile same. Ne žele da ijedna majka bude ranjena kao one.

Iza toga stoji i osobno iskustvo samoće. Gošća prenosi njihove riječi: „U vrijeme kad sam ja imala pobačaj, da je barem netko bio ispred bolnice s plakatom na kojem piše *Trudna si, trebaš pomoć* i brojem mobitela.“ Umjesto toga nije bilo nikoga. Poslodavac je ženi rekao da se neće moći vratiti na posao. Muž joj je rekao „pobacit ćeš“ ili „učini što ti hoćeš“. Zbog takve ravnodušnosti izgubila je tlo pod nogama i, kako zaključuje Marija Šošić, zapravo nije imala drugog izbora.

Slavko Blažić se slaže. Ističe da je lako dijagnosticirati problem i osuditi čovjeka, ali da je svakoga nešto dovelo do toga da postane ono što jest. To nije opravdanje za grijeh, naglašava, i grijeh treba nazvati grijehom. Ipak, djeci na vjeronauku često kaže: „Kad vidite nekog alkoholičara, možda ga nitko nikada zagrlio nije.“ Radu Centra odaje priznanje riječima da Centar „onima koji su oduzeli život daje novi život“.

Voditelj priznaje i da je bio iznenađen. Mislio je da molitelji samo „vuku žene za rukave“ da ne pobace, a o ovom dijelu rada nigdje nije čitao. Iako je, kako kaže u šali, rijetko bez riječi, ovo svjedočanstvo naziva prekrasnim i dirljivim.
sections.subtitle_en: "Freed by Forgiveness": from the wound to prayer for other mothers
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the spiritual-psychological help program "Freed by Forgiveness"
sections.content_en:
For women wounded by abortion, the Center launched the program **"Freed by Forgiveness"**. Marija Šošić describes it as **spiritual-psychological help** conducted in the form of spiritual exercises. Women contemplate the Word of God and approach sacramental life. In this way, they arrive at the experience of God's liberating mercy and can, as she says, "live in the freedom of the Child of God".

After the program, many actively get involved in the **Apostolate for Life**. Most often they join the prayer warriors in front of the hospital and pray for other children and mothers in the situation in which they once were themselves. They do not want any mother to be wounded as they were.

Behind that also stands a personal experience of loneliness. The guest conveys their words: "At the time when I had an abortion, if only someone had been in front of the hospital with a poster saying *You are pregnant, you need help* and a mobile phone number." Instead, there was no one. The employer told the woman that she would not be able to return to work. Her husband told her "you will abort" or "do what you want". Due to such indifference, she lost the ground beneath her feet and, as Marija Šošić concludes, actually had no other choice.

Slavko Blažić agrees. He points out that it is easy to diagnose a problem and condemn a person, but that something brought everyone to become what they are. That is not an excuse for sin, he emphasizes, and sin should be called sin. Still, he often tells children in religious education class: "When you see an alcoholic, maybe no one has ever embraced him." He pays tribute to the Center's work with the words that the Center "gives new life to those who took a life".

The host also admits that he was surprised. He thought that prayer warriors merely "pull women by their sleeves" so they would not abort, and about this part of the work he had read nowhere. Although, as he says in jest, he is rarely at a loss for words, he calls this testimony beautiful and moving.
keywords_en: prayer warriors in front of the hospital

sections.subtitle: „Sakrament Sotone“: duhovna pozadina pobačaja i žene koje su prevarene
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić govori o molitvi i postu kao temelju inicijative
sections.content:
Slavko Blažić sažima tko sve dolazi u Centar: žene koje razmišljaju o pobačaju, one koje su već pobacile te one bez materijalne pomoći i podrške supruga. Zatim postavlja ključno pitanje: što osim ranjenosti, neimaštine i osjećaja napuštenosti vodi ženu prema pobačaju? Postoji li **duhovna pozadina**?

Podsjeća na objavu o pobačaju kao **„sakramentu Sotone“** i objašnjava usporedbu. Riječi „ovo je moje tijelo“ u kršćanstvu označavaju Isusovo tijelo koje se predaje za druge. U pobačaju se, naprotiv, nekome tijelo oduzima.

Marija Šošić potvrđuje da duhovna pozadina postoji. Zato, kaže, neprijatelji nisu oni koji o udruzi govore negativno. Riječ je o duhovnoj stvarnosti, a s njom se nose ponajprije **molitvom i postom**. Poziva se na Isusove riječi iz Evanđelja da se neki zlodusi ne mogu istjerati drugačije nego molitvom i postom. Molitva i post zato su **prvi stup inicijative**. Kad se majka obrati za pomoć, jamči joj se potpuna diskrecija: s njom razgovara jedna osoba, a cijeli tim u pozadini moli.

Gošća navodi i koliko pomoći nude:
- najam i plaćanje stana i režija
- plaćanje fakulteta do kraja studija
- plaćanje tete čuvalice
- podršku dok majka ne pronađe posao i ne osamostali se

Unatoč svemu, neke žene ipak pobace. Marija Šošić to tumači time da ih je „neprijatelj Božji nadvladao“ i prevario. Takve su žene, smatra, **prevarene**.

Iz iskustva tvrdi da ne postoji žena koja je sretna što je pobacila. Gotovo sve, kaže, idu na pobačaj sa suzama jer znaju da se događa nešto iznimno važno i nepovratno. Nasuprot tome, svaka majka koja je izabrala život, koliko god joj situacija bila teška, danas radosno svjedoči o tome i svoje dijete ne bi dala nikome na svijetu.

Među čestim razlozima navodi **nepotpune informacije**. Ženama se govori da je riječ o „kratkom zahvatu“ ili „samo jednoj tableti“, a nitko im ne kaže što dolazi poslije.

Najteže joj je izgovoriti sljedeću činjenicu: **najveći broj pobačaja događa se unutar obitelji**, kod žena koje su već majke. Dugo je vremena statistika pokazivala da je riječ najčešće o **trećem djetetu**. Slavko Blažić se prisjeća da je to spominjao i profesor Mužić, koji mu je predavao na KBF-u. Priznaje da ga je ta spoznaja šokirala, jer te žene gledaju svoju prethodnu djecu.
sections.subtitle_en: "The Sacrament of Satan": the spiritual background of abortion and women who are deceived
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić speaks about prayer and fasting as the foundation of the initiative
sections.content_en:
Slavko Blažić summarizes all who come to the Center: women considering abortion, those who have already had an abortion, and those without material help and husband's support. Then he asks a key question: what besides woundedness, poverty, and feelings of abandonment leads a woman toward abortion? Is there a **spiritual background**?

He recalls the revelation about abortion as the **"sacrament of Satan"** and explains the comparison. The words "this is my body" in Christianity designate the body of Jesus that is given up for others. In abortion, on the contrary, someone's body is taken away.

Marija Šošić confirms that a spiritual background exists. That is why, she says, the enemies are not those who speak negatively about the association. It is a matter of a spiritual reality, and they cope with it primarily **through prayer and fasting**. She refers to the words of Jesus from the Gospel that certain demons cannot be driven out except by prayer and fasting. Prayer and fasting are therefore the **first pillar of the initiative**. When a mother turns for help, complete discretion is guaranteed to her: one person speaks with her, while the entire team in the background prays.

The guest also states how much help they offer:
- renting and paying for an apartment and utilities
- paying for college until the end of studies
- paying for a babysitter
- support until the mother finds a job and becomes independent

Despite everything, some women still abort. Marija Šošić interprets this by the fact that the "enemy of God overcame them" and deceived them. Such women, she considers, are **deceived**.

From experience, she asserts that there is no woman who is happy that she aborted. Almost all of them, she says, go to an abortion in tears because they know that something exceptionally important and irreversible is happening. In contrast, every mother who chose life, however difficult her situation was, today joyfully testifies about it and would not give her child to anyone in the world.

Among the frequent reasons, she lists **incomplete information**. Women are told that it is a matter of a "short procedure" or "just one pill", and no one tells them what comes after.

The hardest thing for her to utter is the following fact: **the largest number of abortions happens within families**, among women who are already mothers. For a long time, statistics showed that it was most often a matter of a **third child**. Slavko Blažić recalls that Professor Mužić, who taught him at the Catholic Faculty of Theology (KBF), also mentioned this. He admits that this realization shocked him, because those women look at their previous children.

sections.subtitle: Zakon, škola i znanost: zašto promjena mora početi od svijesti
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o otkucajima srca djeteta vidljivima na ultrazvuku
sections.content:
Slavko Blažić otvara pitanje **uloge države i društva**. Tragedijom naziva činjenicu da u društvu u kojem, kako kaže, više od 20 godina vladaju demokršćani, zakon dopušta pobačaj do desetog tjedna. To mu je neobjašnjivo.

Voditelj iskreno priznaje i da **nije siguran bi li referendum o pobačaju danas prošao**. Razlog vidi u ideologiji koja stoji iza te teme i u brojnim napadima, što opisuje kao „baš sotonski“. Kaže da poznaje mnogo vjeroučitelja i političara. Čini mu se da su se, što su više napredovali, više prilagođavali, iako vjeruje da neki ipak pokušavaju nešto učiniti. Kao pozitivan primjer navodi **ministra Šipića**, za kojeg kaže da je, prema njegovu mišljenju, prvi ministar koji je javno sudjelovao u Hodu za život. To smatra velikim korakom.

Ipak, ocjenjuje da su društvo i država u ovom pitanju „mlaki“. Pobačaj se prikazuje kao nešto normalno. Prisjeća se da se još u gimnaziji učilo da je pobačaj u Hrvatskoj dopušten do desetog tjedna, što Marija Šošić potvrđuje.

Gošća prihvaća sve što je rečeno o zakonu, ali predlaže da se vrati „nekoliko koraka unazad“, do **mijenjanja svijesti ljudi**. Dugo se, kaže, tvrdilo da je dijete u majčinoj utrobi samo komad tkiva i da nije živo. Danas suvremena tehnologija, ponajprije **ultrazvuk**, jasno pokazuje da to nije istina.

Naglašava da to nije izum Crkve niti samo vjerski stav, nego znanstvena činjenica. Djetetu srce počinje kucati **već između 18. i 21. dana od začeća**, a riječ je o živom biću od samog začeća, ne od nekog tjedna ili mjeseca. Ironično pita koji bi to trenutak trebao biti: „Kad odzvoni ponoć, pa onda kreće sljedeći dan, aha, onda više nije dozvoljeno pobaciti jer sad si čovjek?“

Upravo je to, objašnjava, razlog **bdijenja pred bolnicom**. Molitelji žele osvijestiti ljude o svetosti ljudskog života i vrijednosti svakog začetog djeteta, jer „nitko od nas nije viška“. Bog je svaki život stvorio s planom, svejedno je li dijete ljudima željeno, jer ga je Bog poželio. Kroz 12 godina, zaključuje, vidi se da se svijest polako mijenja, ali za promjenu cijelog društva trebat će još vremena.
sections.subtitle_en: Law, school, and science: why change must begin from consciousness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the child's heartbeat visible on ultrasound
sections.content_en:
Slavko Blažić opens the question of the **role of the state and society**. He calls it a tragedy that in a society where, as he says, Christian Democrats have ruled for more than 20 years, the law permits abortion up to the tenth week. To him, that is inexplicable.

The host also honestly admits that **he is not sure whether a referendum on abortion would pass today**. He sees the reason in the ideology standing behind that topic and in numerous attacks, which he describes as "truly satanic". He says he knows many religious education teachers and politicians. It seems to him that the more they advanced, the more they adapted, although he believes that some nevertheless try to do something. As a positive example, he cites **Minister Šipić**, whom he says is, in his opinion, the first minister who publicly participated in the Walk for Life. He considers that a big step.

Nevertheless, he assesses that society and the state are "lukewarm" on this issue. Abortion is portrayed as something normal. He recalls that back in gymnasium it was taught that abortion in Croatia is permitted up to the tenth week, which Marija Šošić confirms.

The guest accepts everything said about the law, but proposes going back "several steps", to **changing people's consciousness**. For a long time, she says, it was claimed that a child in the mother's womb is just a piece of tissue and not alive. Today, modern technology, primarily **ultrasound**, clearly shows that this is not true.

She emphasizes that this is not an invention of the Church nor merely a religious stance, but a scientific fact. A child's heart begins to beat **already between the 18th and 21st day from conception**, and it is a living being from conception itself, not from some week or month. She ironically asks what that moment should be: "When midnight strikes, and then the next day starts, aha, then it is no longer permitted to abort because now you are a human being?"

That is precisely, she explains, the reason for the **vigil in front of the hospital**. The prayer warriors want to make people conscious of the sanctity of human life and the value of every conceived child, because "none of us is surplus". God created every life with a plan, regardless of whether the child is desired by humans, because God desired it. Through 12 years, she concludes, it is evident that consciousness is slowly changing, but changing the whole society will take more time.
keywords_en: vigil in front of the hospital

sections.subtitle: Obitelji s više djece nisu socijalni slučajevi: grupe podrške i molitvene kampanje
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić opisuje molitvenu kampanju posvećenu djeci s Downovim sindromom
sections.content:
Kao znak postupne promjene svijesti Marija Šošić navodi sve brojnije **obiteljske zajednice i grupe podrške za majke**. U Splitu djeluje inicijativa **Mame za mame**, odnosno **Majke u zagrljaju majke**, gdje se majke na susretima međusobno podržavaju.

S druge strane, na društvenim mrežama čim se otvori ta tema stižu „grozni komentari“, primjerice na objave inicijativa **Život više** i **Brojne obitelji**. Pomake države smatra pohvalnima, ali i „tek kapi u moru“ onoga što bi trebalo učiniti za majke, trudnice i obitelji s više djece.

Posebno upozorava na **stigmatizaciju brojnih obitelji**. U Centar dolaze majke koje trpe kritike jer su ponovno zatrudnjele, iako već imaju dvoje ili troje djece. Neke su izložene i izrugivanju na poslu, kao da je riječ o nečem nazadnom. Obitelji sa sedmero ili osmero djece prikazuju se kao „slučajni slučajevi“. Gošća smatra da je to zapravo ljepota i uzor: obitelji s više djece nisu socijalni slučajevi, nego hrabre obitelji otvorene životu od kojih se može mnogo naučiti.

To se odražava i u **molitvenim kampanjama**. Uz temeljne nakane, molitvu za prestanak pobačaja, pomoć majkama, molitvu za ranjene pobačajem te za obraćenje onih koji pobačaj izvršavaju i podržavaju, svaka kampanja ima i posebnu temu:
- **djeca s Downovim sindromom**: kroz tribine i svjedočanstva roditelja javnosti se pokazuje da otkriće na ultrazvuku ne smije automatski značiti pobačaj. Roditelji su svjedočili da uz izazove ta djeca donose ljepotu, blagoslov i radost te da „nikako nisu viška na ovom svijetu“.
- **„Za dijete više“**: kampanja je, kaže gošća, urodila plodom. Neki volonteri s dvoje ili troje djece, koji su se bojali novog života, javljali su se s viješću da je u obitelji četvrta trudnoća i zahvaljivali na ohrabrenju.
- **mnogobrojne hrvatske obitelji**: s nadom da Hrvatska bude „prepuna djecom, da vrvi djecom“, što je, kaže, moguće jedino s brojnim obiteljima.
sections.subtitle_en: Families with multiple children are not welfare cases: support groups and prayer campaigns
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić describes a prayer campaign dedicated to children with Down syndrome
sections.content_en:
As a sign of the gradual change of consciousness, Marija Šošić cites increasingly numerous **family communities and support groups for mothers**. In Split, the initiative **Mame za mame**, that is, **Majke u zagrljaju majke**, operates, where mothers support one another at gatherings.

On the other hand, on social networks as soon as that topic is opened, "horrible comments" arrive, for instance on posts of the initiatives **Život više** and **Brojne obitelji**. She considers the moves of the state commendable, but also "only a drop in the ocean" of what should be done for mothers, pregnant women, and families with multiple children.

She particularly warns about the **stigmatization of large families**. Mothers who endure criticism because they became pregnant again, even though they already have two or three children, come to the Center. Some are exposed to mockery at work as well, as if it were a matter of something backward. Families with seven or eight children are portrayed as "welfare cases". The guest considers that this is actually beauty and an example: families with multiple children are not welfare cases, but courageous families open to life from whom much can be learned.

This is also reflected in **prayer campaigns**. Along with fundamental intentions, prayer for an end to abortion, help for mothers, prayer for those wounded by abortion, and for the conversion of those who perform and support abortion, each campaign also has a special theme:
- **children with Down syndrome**: through panels and parents' testimonies, it is shown to the public that a discovery on ultrasound must not automatically mean abortion. Parents testified that alongside challenges, those children bring beauty, blessing, and joy, and that they are "by no means surplus in this world".
- **"For One More Child"**: the campaign, says the guest, bore fruit. Some volunteers with two or three children, who were afraid of new life, reached out with the news that a fourth pregnancy was underway in the family and thanked them for the encouragement.
- **large Croatian families**: with the hope that Croatia be "overflowing with children, teeming with children", which is, she says, possible only with large families.

sections.subtitle: Najteža pitanja: bolesno dijete, silovanje i priča o Mihaeli
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća svjedoči o najboljoj prijateljici začetoj silovanjem
sections.content:
Slavko Blažić prelazi na takozvane teške slučajeve. Prisjeća se događaja od prije dvije-tri godine, kad se jedna žena javno pobunila jer joj nije odobren pobačaj u kasnijoj fazi trudnoće zbog bolesti djeteta. Kaže da nije mogao vjerovati kako ju je društvo prikazalo kao heroinu jer „ne želi da njezino dijete pati“.

Naglašava da joj ne želi suditi i ne zna što prolazi. Ipak ga je začudilo što je i sama dosljedno govorila o djetetu. Postavlja pitanje: ako dijete od deset godina oboli, zašto bi tu vrijedila drukčija logika? Marija Šošić to ironično dovršava riječima „da ne pati, sad ćemo ga…“. Voditelj zaključuje da je jedina razlika u tome što se jedno dijete vidi, a drugo ne. Zatim pita i o klasičnom argumentu silovanja.

Gošća silovanje naziva **najgorim činom i najgorom tragedijom koja se može dogoditi jednoj ženi**. Ipak smatra da **pobačaj neće izliječiti njezinu ranu**. Ženi treba pomoći da se suoči s tom ranom i izađe iz goleme traume. Upozorava i na nerazmjer: počinitelj, ako ga se uopće privede i osudi, dobije nekoliko godina zatvora, a dijete, koje ničim nije krivo, dobije smrtnu kaznu.

Zatim iznosi osobno svjedočanstvo. Njezina **najbolja prijateljica začeta je silovanjem**, a to je saznala u kasnim dvadesetima. Bio je to golem šok, ali kasnije i zahvalnost: majci koja ju je rodila, obitelji koja ju je prigrlila i podigla te ocu koji ju je prihvatio iako nije njegova kći. Danas je **majka sedmero djece i šesterostruka baka**. „Pa tko može reći da je Mihaela viška na ovom svijetu“ zbog strašnog čina njezina oca, pita Marija Šošić.

Slavko Blažić naglašava da je silovanje jedan od najgnusnijih zločina i da to nije upitno. Želi samo reći da se odgovorom zlom na zlo zlo samo širi. Gošća dodaje da pobačaj ni tada neće izliječiti majku. Naprotiv, otvorit će joj **novu ranu, ranu od pobačaja**.
sections.subtitle_en: The hardest questions: a sick child, rape, and the story of Mihaela
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest testifies about her best friend conceived by rape
sections.content_en:
Slavko Blažić moves on to so-called difficult cases. He recalls an event from two or three years ago, when a woman publicly rebelled because she was not granted an abortion in a later stage of pregnancy due to the child's illness. He says he could not believe how society portrayed her as a heroine because "she does not want her child to suffer".

He emphasizes that he does not want to judge her and does not know what she is going through. Nevertheless, it surprised him that she herself consistently spoke of a child. He poses the question: if a child of ten years falls ill, why would a different logic apply there? Marija Šošić ironically finishes that with the words "so that it does not suffer, now we will...". The host concludes that the only difference is that one child is seen, and the other is not. Then he also asks about the classic argument of rape.

The guest calls rape **the worst act and the worst tragedy that can happen to a woman**. Nevertheless, she considers that **abortion will not heal her wound**. The woman needs to be helped to face that wound and emerge from immense trauma. She also warns of the disproportion: the perpetrator, if he is apprehended and convicted at all, receives a few years in prison, while the child, who is guilty of nothing, receives the death penalty.

Then she presents a personal testimony. Her **best friend was conceived by rape**, and she found that out in her late twenties. It was an immense shock, but later also gratitude: to the mother who gave birth to her, to the family who embraced and raised her, and to the father who accepted her even though she is not his daughter. Today she is a **mother of seven children and a six-time grandmother**. "Why, who can say that Mihaela is surplus in this world" because of the terrible act of her father, asks Marija Šošić.

Slavko Blažić emphasizes that rape is one of the most heinous crimes and that that is not questionable. He only wants to say that responding with evil to evil only spreads evil. The guest adds that abortion even then will not heal the mother. On the contrary, it will open **a new wound, the wound of abortion**, for her.

sections.subtitle: Prevencija počinje u obitelji: prava bez odgovornosti ne postoje
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić ističe obitelj kao prvo mjesto moralnog odgoja mladih
sections.content:
Razgovor se okreće **prevenciji i odgoju mladih**. Slavko Blažić prenosi ono što govori učenicima: neka ne rade ono za što nisu spremni kasnije preuzeti odgovornost. Tko smatra da je spreman na spolni čin, mora biti spreman i na njegove posljedice. Problem vidi u društvu koje posljedice izbjegava i stalno ističe „moja prava, moja prava“. Marija Šošić to dopunjuje: „Ali nema odgovornosti.“

Gošća se slaže da je prevencija u odgoju mladih ključna, a posebno je važna na **vjeronauku**. To je tema koju, kaže, „ne bi smio nijedan vjeroučitelj promaći“. Ako mladi to ne nauče na vjeronauku, otići će na druga mjesta gdje neće dobiti prave informacije i gdje ih se može odvesti u propast.

Ipak, naglašava da je prevencija **najpotrebnija u obitelji**. Ondje mladi trebaju dobiti prvo iskustvo moralnog odgoja. Zdrava obitelj, u okruženju ljubavi i međusobnog poštovanja, ishodište je svega. Nakon obitelji važnu ulogu imaju škola, vjeroučitelji, nastavnici i sve sredine u kojima dijete sudjeluje u društvenom životu. Ako ondje ne dobije prave informacije, upozorava, potražit će ih kod drugih ili na internetu, gdje će čitati neistine koje ga vode u krivom smjeru.
sections.subtitle_en: Prevention begins in the family: rights without responsibilities do not exist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić highlights the family as the first place of moral education of youth
sections.content_en:
The conversation turns to **prevention and the education of youth**. Slavko Blažić conveys what he tells students: let them not do what they are not ready to take responsibility for later. Whoever considers that they are ready for the sexual act must also be ready for its consequences. He sees the problem in a society that avoids consequences and constantly emphasizes "my rights, my rights". Marija Šošić supplements that: "But there is no responsibility."

The guest agrees that prevention in the education of youth is crucial, and is especially important in **religious education class**. That is a topic that, she says, "no religious education teacher should miss". If youth do not learn that in religious education class, they will go to other places where they will not receive true information and where they can be led to ruin.

Nevertheless, she emphasizes that prevention is **most needed in the family**. There youth should receive the first experience of moral education. A healthy family, in an environment of love and mutual respect, is the origin of everything. After the family, an important role is played by school, religious education teachers, instructors, and all environments in which the child participates in social life. If they do not receive the right information there, she warns, they will seek it from others or on the internet, where they will read untruths leading them in the wrong direction.

sections.subtitle: Zaboravljeni očevi: od oduzetog očinstva do „napravi kako hoćeš“
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava da za pobačaj nije potreban potpis oca djeteta
sections.content:
Slavko Blažić otvara temu **prava očeva**. Stalno se govori o pravima žene i djeteta, a gdje je pravo oca? Pita koliko očeva uopće ne zna da je njihovo dijete pobačeno. Priznaje da neki očevi nažalost i sami potiču pobačaj. Povlači i paralelu s razvodima, gdje majka, kako kaže, ima primarno pravo na odgoj, a očevi „pravo na vikende“. „Moja kćer je jednako kćer moja kao i moje žene“, ističe. Ne niječe muku poroda kroz koju je prošla njegova supruga, ali pita zašto je to tako.

Marija Šošić naziva očeve **„stvoriteljima života“** i ističe da su uloge majke i oca podjednako važne. U Centar se, kaže, javljaju očevi s različitim iskustvima:
- **očevi koji naknadno saznaju** da je njihova supruga ili djevojka bila trudna i pobacila. Osjećaju da im je oduzeto pravo na očinstvo jer nisu ništa mogli reći.
- **očevi koji se protive pobačaju**, ali na odluku ne mogu utjecati. Prema zakonu u bolnici je dovoljan potpis žene, a oca se ništa ne pita.
- **očevi koji su ženu ostavili bez podrške** riječima „napravi kako hoćeš, to je tvoje tijelo, ti odluči“. Time je izostala, kako kaže gošća, njihova muževnost i zaštitnička uloga, a žena je izgubila uporište i pobacila. Neki od njih danas se kaju.
- **očevi koji su ženu prisilili** ultimatumom „ili pobačaj ili se razilazimo“.

Naknadno, kaže, većina shvati, a najčešće žene, da ga nisu trebale slušati, nego potražiti pomoć. Danas postoje različite udruge i sigurne kuće.

Kao primjer navodi program za žene ranjene pobačajem održan prethodnog tjedna u Dalmaciji. Jedna je sudionica ispričala: „Pa ja bih stvarno rodila, ali on je jednostavno rekao: ako ti ćeš roditi, ti se sama misli za sebe i to dijete.“ Nije imala novca, posla ni ikoga kome bi se obratila, a brinula se i kako će s djecom koju je već imala ako je muž ostavi. Danas pred bolnicom stoji natpis „Trudna si, trebaš pomoć“ s brojem mobitela i poruka „Nisi sama“. Te su dvije riječi, smatra gošća, **najvažnije u spašavanju jednog života**.

Voditelj kaže da donekle može razumjeti strah i nedostatak hrabrosti kod petnaestogodišnjakinja i šesnaestogodišnjakinja, ali ga i dalje zapanjuje da češće pobacuju one koje su već majke. Marija Šošić tu se ponovno vraća na duhovnu pozadinu. Ako je znanost jasno pokazala kad život počinje, rasprave više ne bi smjelo biti. Pogotovo je to tako kod roditelja kojima su živa djeca velika radost, a sljedeće dijete iz straha ili zbog okolnosti postane „viška“. Upravo zato, zaključuje, Centar postoji: da ohrabri, uputi i pomogne izaći iz krize.
sections.subtitle_en: Forgotten fathers: from stripped fatherhood to "do as you want"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that the signature of the child's father is not required for an abortion
sections.content_en:
Slavko Blažić opens the topic of **fathers' rights**. People constantly talk about the rights of the woman and the child, but where is the father's right? He asks how many fathers do not even know that their child was aborted. He admits that some fathers unfortunately also encourage abortion themselves. He also draws a parallel with divorces, where the mother, as he says, has the primary right to upbringing, and fathers "the right to weekends". "My daughter is just as much my daughter as she is my wife's," he points out. He does not deny the agony of childbirth through which his wife went, but asks why it is so.

Marija Šošić calls fathers **"creators of life"** and emphasizes that the roles of mother and father are equally important. At the Center, she says, fathers with different experiences reach out:
- **fathers who subsequently find out** that their wife or girlfriend was pregnant and had an abortion. They feel that their right to fatherhood was stripped because they could say nothing.
- **fathers who oppose abortion**, but cannot influence the decision. According to the law in the hospital, the woman's signature is sufficient, and the father is asked nothing.
- **fathers who left the woman without support** with the words "do as you want, that is your body, you decide". Thereby, as the guest says, their manhood and protective role was absent, and the woman lost her footing and had an abortion. Some of them today repent.
- **fathers who forced the woman** with the ultimatum "either abortion or we part ways".

Subsequently, she says, most realize, and most frequently women, that they should not have listened to him, but sought help. Today various associations and safe houses exist.

As an example, she cites a program for women wounded by abortion held the previous week in Dalmatia. One participant recounted: "Why, I really would have given birth, but he simply said: if you will give birth, you think for yourself and that child alone." She had no money, no job, nor anyone to turn to, and she also worried about how she would manage with the children she already had if her husband left her. Today in front of the hospital stands the sign "You are pregnant, you need help" with a mobile phone number and the message "You are not alone". Those four words, the guest considers, are **the most important in saving a single life**.

The host says that to some extent he can understand fear and lack of courage among fifteen-year-olds and sixteen-year-olds, but it still astounds him that those who are already mothers more frequently abort. Marija Šošić here returns again to the spiritual background. If science clearly showed when life begins, discussion should no longer exist. Especially is that so among parents for whom living children are a great joy, and the next child out of fear or due to circumstances becomes "surplus". Precisely that is why, she concludes, the Center exists: to encourage, guide, and help emerge from crisis.

sections.subtitle: Noćna straža i dječak Angelo: priča o sezonskoj radnici koja je odabrala život
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić prepričava jutro u kojem je trudnica otkazala zakazani pobačaj
sections.content:
Na voditeljevu molbu da ispriča jednu konkretnu životnu priču bez imena, Marija Šošić najprije iznosi brojku. Od početka djelovanja inicijative zna se za **200 spašenih dječjih života**. Riječ je samo o majkama koje su zatražile pomoć ili posvjedočile da su se predomislile zbog prisutnosti molitelja. Stvarni broj spašenih, kaže, „zna se tek u nebu“.

Zatim pripovijeda slučaj koji ju se posebno dojmio. Mlada djevojka došla je na **sezonski rad na jedan dalmatinski otok**, zaljubila se u mladića i zatrudnjela. On joj je rekao da nije spreman biti otac, iako to već jest jer je dijete tu, i da s njom može ostati samo ako pobaci. Voditelj to ironično komentira: „Hrabro muški.“

Djevojka je otišla u ginekološku ordinaciju po uputnicu za pobačaj. U čekaonici je razgovarala sa ženom koja je **deset godina pokušavala začeti** i došla po uputnicu za pretrage u Splitu ili Zagrebu. Djevojka joj je, kao da ide vaditi krv, rekla zašto je došla. Žena se jako rastužila i rekla: „Pa nemoj to učiniti, pa daj ga meni.“ Djevojka je odbila, rekavši da će dijete, ako ga rodi, odgajati sama. Žena je potom na internetu pronašla kontakt Centra i nazvala Mariju Šošić. Na njezin prijedlog pozvala je djevojku na kavu i ponudila joj pomoć, a djevojka je pristala na razgovor.

Slijedio je **tjedan svakodnevnih razgovora**. Djevojka je govorila o strahovima: neće moći raditi sezonu, roditelji će je izbaciti iz kuće i razočarati se u nju. Kad bi je ohrabrila i pokazala joj drukčiji scenarij u kojem je to samo privremena kriza, djevojka bi počela smišljati imena za dijete. Ipak, stalno se vraćala društvu koje joj je govorilo da „nije normalna“, da ne može roditi dijete čovjeku koji ju je ostavio i da su sumnjivi ljudi koji nude pomoć. Gošća primjećuje da je danas neobično kad netko nudi **bezuvjetnu pomoć**, a ništa ne traži zauzvrat.

Sedmog dana stigla je poruka: „Hvala za sve, međutim, ja sutra imam zakazan pobačaj, ja to uistinu ne mogu.“ Za takve trenutke Centar ima, kako kaže, „skrivenu žrtvicu“, **noćnu stražu**. Molitvena grupa, ne znajući o kome je riječ, smjenjuje se cijelu noć po sat vremena u svojim domovima. Mole za dijete i za dušu majke.

Ujutro, u vrijeme zakazanog termina, kad je mislila da je sve gotovo, Marija Šošić dobila je poruku: „Nazvala sam kliniku, neću to učiniti. Ne znam zašto, ali rodit ću, može sve to što ste mi ponudili.“ Gošća to tumači **moći molitve**. Bog, kaže, ima zadnju riječ jer je ovo njegova bitka, već dobivena na križu, a molitelji su njegova produžena ruka.

Dogodilo se sve čega se djevojka bojala. Mladić je ustrajao u odbijanju, a roditelji su je odbacili. Smještena je u sestrinsku **udrugu Betlehem**, kuću koja joj je nekoliko mjeseci pružala krov nad glavom i sve potrebno. Za Božić su je roditelji ipak posjetili. Kad su ugledali trbuščić, „raspali su se“, shvatili da je to njihovo unuče i pozvali je kući. Problem, ističe gošća, nikad nije bio financijski, nego razočaranje.

Rodio se dječak **Angelo**. Djelatnici Centra bili su pozvani na krštenje i s majkom su i danas u kontaktu. Ona im javlja njegove školske uspjehe i izvanškolske aktivnosti, a Angelo sada ide u drugi razred. Majka je, zaključuje Marija Šošić, presretna, a Centar je bio uz nju kad se našla pred zidom i mislila da je pobačaj jedino rješenje. Slavko Blažić kaže da bi razgovor imao smisla i da su čuli samo tu priču.
sections.subtitle_en: Night watch and the boy Angelo: the story of a seasonal worker who chose life
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić recounts the morning in which a pregnant woman canceled a scheduled abortion
sections.content_en:
At the host's request to tell one concrete life story without names, Marija Šošić first presents a figure. Since the beginning of the initiative's activity, **200 saved children's lives** are known of. It is a matter only of mothers who requested help or testified that they changed their minds because of the presence of prayer warriors. The actual number of those saved, she says, "is known only in heaven".

Then she narrates a case that particularly moved her. A young girl came for **seasonal work on a Dalmatian island**, fell in love with a young man, and became pregnant. He told her that he was not ready to be a father, even though he already is because the child is here, and that he can stay with her only if she aborts. The host ironically comments on that: "Bravely manly."

The girl went to a gynecological office for a referral for an abortion. In the waiting room, she spoke with a woman who had been **trying to conceive for ten years** and came for a referral for examinations in Split or Zagreb. The girl, as if going to have blood drawn, told her why she had come. The woman became very sad and said: "Well, don't do that, why, give him to me." The girl refused, saying that if she gives birth to the child, she will raise it alone. The woman then found the Center's contact on the internet and called Marija Šošić. At her suggestion, she invited the girl for coffee and offered her help, and the girl agreed to a conversation.

A **week of daily conversations** followed. The girl spoke about her fears: she would not be able to work the season, her parents would kick her out of the house and be disappointed in her. When she would encourage her and show her a different scenario in which that is only a temporary crisis, the girl would begin inventing names for the child. Still, she constantly returned to company that told her she was "not normal", that she could not give birth to a child for a man who left her, and that the people offering help were suspicious. The guest notes that today it is unusual when someone offers **unconditional help**, and asks for nothing in return.

On the seventh day, a message arrived: "Thank you for everything, however, I have a scheduled abortion tomorrow, I truly cannot do this." For such moments, the Center has, as she says, a "hidden little sacrifice", the **night watch**. The prayer group, not knowing who it is about, takes turns all night for an hour at a time in their homes. They pray for the child and for the soul of the mother.

In the morning, at the time of the scheduled appointment, when she thought everything was over, Marija Šošić received a message: "I called the clinic, I will not do that. I do not know why, but I will give birth, everything that you offered me is fine." The guest interprets this by the **power of prayer**. God, she says, has the final word because this is His battle, already won on the Cross, and the prayer warriors are His extended arm.

Everything the girl feared happened. The young man persisted in refusal, and the parents rejected her. She was accommodated in the sister **association Betlehem**, a house that provided her with a roof over her head and everything necessary for several months. For Christmas, her parents nevertheless visited her. When they beheld the little belly, they "broke down", realized that it was their grandchild, and invited her home. The problem, points out the guest, was never financial, but disappointment.

A baby boy, **Angelo**, was born. The staff of the Center were invited to the baptism and are still in contact with the mother today. She reports his school successes and extracurricular activities to them, and Angelo is now in the second grade. The mother is, Marija Šošić concludes, overjoyed, and the Center was by her side when she found herself up against a wall and thought that abortion was the only solution. Slavko Blažić says that the conversation would have had meaning even if they had heard only that story.

sections.subtitle: „Kriza je privremena, a pobačaj je zauvijek“: poruka trudnicama
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća upućuje poruku ohrabrenja trudnicama u dvojbi
sections.content:
Pri kraju razgovora Slavko Blažić traži od gošće poruku i praktične savjete za trudnice koje razmišljaju o pobačaju.

Marija Šošić svjesna je da svaka majka neće skupiti hrabrosti prići moliteljima pred bolnicom i reći da je trudna i da želi pobaciti. No mnoge će nazvati **broj istaknut na mjestu bdijenja**. Ponekad to učini netko blizak, tko primijeti da se majka dvoumi i želi joj pomoći, pa je poveže s Centrom.

Centar je, naglašava, **dostupan 24 sata na dan**. Kontakt se u svakom trenutku može pronaći na **Facebook stranici Centar za život Split** i na Instagramu Centra.

Njezina je poruka jasna: **pobačaj nikada nije rješenje**. Centar nudi pomoć „kao produženi član obitelji“. To zaista i postanu majkama koje im se obrate: prate ih kad se osjećaju same, saslušaju ih i nude rješenja prema njihovim potrebama. „Kriza je privremena, a pobačaj je zauvijek“, ističe gošća.

Svako dijete, zaključuje, zaslužuje život. Svaka majka zaslužuje sigurno okruženje u kojem će dijete donijeti na svijet. Odgovornost za to ne vidi samo u Centru za život i udruzi Hrvatska za život, nego u cijelom društvu. Ono treba majci pomoći da rodi, ali i poslije u odgoju djeteta, kako bi oboje imali dostojanstven život.
sections.subtitle_en: "A crisis is temporary, but abortion is forever": a message to pregnant women
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest addresses a message of encouragement to pregnant women in doubt
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the conversation, Slavko Blažić asks the guest for a message and practical advice for pregnant women considering abortion.

Marija Šošić is aware that not every mother will muster the courage to approach the prayer warriors in front of the hospital and say that she is pregnant and wants an abortion. But many will call the **number displayed at the vigil site**. Sometimes someone close does that, someone who notices that the mother is hesitating and wants to help her, so connects her with the Center.

The Center is, she emphasizes, **available 24 hours a day**. The contact can be found at any time on the **Facebook page Centar za život Split** and on the Center's Instagram.

Her message is clear: **abortion is never the solution**. The Center offers help "as an extended family member". They truly become that to mothers who reach out to them: they accompany them when they feel alone, listen to them, and offer solutions according to their needs. "A crisis is temporary, but abortion is forever," emphasizes the guest.

Every child, she concludes, deserves life. Every mother deserves a safe environment in which to bring a child into the world. She sees responsibility for this not only in the Center for Life and the association Hrvatska za život, but in the entire society. It should help the mother to give birth, but also afterward in raising the child, so that both have a dignified life.

sections.subtitle: Straža svetog Josipa, pelene i molitva: kako svatko može pomoći
sections.screenshot_description: Marija Šošić nabraja načine na koje javnost može pomoći Centru za život
sections.content:
Na kraju voditelj pita kako gledatelji mogu pomoći radu Centra. Marija Šošić odgovara da može svatko tko ima ljubavi za nerođene i želi širiti kulturu života. Navodi nekoliko oblika pomoći:
- **volontiranje i stručna pomoć**: profesionalci i volonteri koji svojim znanjem i vremenom pomažu majkama.
- **Straža svetog Josipa**: grupa muškaraca koji se okupljaju u Centru na molitvu. Na raspolaganju su i za „muške poslove“ poput selidbi majki te sastavljanja krevetića i ormara. Takvi su volonteri uvijek dobrodošli jer se Centar trenutačno na svom području brine o **više od 50 trudnica**.
- **financijska pomoć**: Centar majkama plaća troškove stanovanja, režije i bonove za hranu.
- **materijalne donacije**: pelene te higijenske potrepštine za dijete i majku.
- **molitva**: ono što je, kako kaže, najpotrebnije. Kroz cijeli razgovor govorilo se o duhovnom boju, a na njega se može odgovoriti samo molitvom, pa je molitvena podrška Centru „itekako potrebna“.

Slavko Blažić zaključuje razgovor obećanjem da će moliti da Bog Centru da snage, a djeci život. Zahvaljuje gošći, a Marija Šošić uzvraća zahvalom na pozivu.
sections.subtitle_en: Saint Joseph's Watch, diapers, and prayer: how anyone can help
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marija Šošić enumerates ways the public can help the Center for Life
sections.content_en:
At the end, the host asks how viewers can help the Center's work. Marija Šošić answers that anyone can who has love for the unborn and wants to spread the culture of life. She lists several forms of help:
- **volunteering and professional assistance**: professionals and volunteers who with their knowledge and time help mothers.
- **Saint Joseph's Watch**: a group of men who gather at the Center for prayer. They are also available for "men's tasks" like moving mothers and assembling cribs and closets. Such volunteers are always welcome because the Center currently cares for **more than 50 pregnant women** in its area.
- **financial assistance**: the Center pays living expenses, utilities, and food vouchers for mothers.
- **material donations**: diapers and hygiene necessities for child and mother.
- **prayer**: that which is, as she says, most needed. Throughout the entire conversation, spiritual warfare was discussed, and it can only be answered by prayer, so prayer support for the Center is "greatly needed".

Slavko Blažić concludes the conversation with a promise that he will pray that God give the Center strength, and the children life. He thanks the guest, and Marija Šošić returns thanks for the invitation.
